assumptions.condition: \(\exists(V_0,V_1):\ V_d\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],\ Y_d=Q_d(V_d)\ (d\in\{0,1\}),\ \mathcal L(V_0\mid U=u)=\mathcal L(V_1\mid U=u)\ \text{for a.e. }u\)

definitions.name: Closed observed-law compatibility polytope
definitions.construction: \(\overline{\mathcal Q}=\{q\in\Delta_{2K-1}^2:(c_0(q),c_1(q))\in\mathbb R_+^{2K}\}\)

definitions.name: Propensity--grid weak-order cells
definitions.construction: \(\Omega(p^{1:L})=\{\omega:\omega\text{ is a weak ordering of }\{0,1,p_0,p_1,p^1,\ldots,p^L\}\text{ consistent with }0<p_0<p_1<1\}\)

definitions.name: Latent-index policy partition
definitions.construction: For \(\omega\in\Omega(p^{1:L})\), \(\mathcal B_\omega=\{[r_{j-1},r_j):j=1,\ldots,m_\omega\}\), where \(0=r_0\le\cdots\le r_{m_\omega}=1\) is the ordering specified by \(\omega\), retaining zero-width tied bins

definitions.name: Order--path component index
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma_K=\Omega(p^{1:L})\times\Sigma_K\), with \(\gamma=(\omega,\sigma)\)

definitions.name: Common-rank allocation fiber
definitions.construction: \(X_\gamma(q)=\{x\ge0:A_\gamma x=b_\gamma+B_\gamma q\}\) with rows \(\sum_sx_{bs}=|I_b|\), \(\sum_{b\in a,s:j_s=k}x_{bs}=a_{1k}\), \(\sum_{b\in c,s:i_s=k}x_{bs}=c_{0k}\), \(\sum_{b\in c,s:j_s=k}x_{bs}=c_{1k}\), and \(\sum_{b\in n,s:i_s=k}x_{bs}=n_{0k}\), for \(\gamma=(\omega,\sigma)\in\Gamma_K\)

definitions.name: Path policy image
definitions.construction: \(S_\gamma(q)=\{C_\gamma x:x\in X_\gamma(q)\}\), where \((C_\gamma x)_\ell=\sum_{b\subseteq[0,p^\ell],s}y_{j_s}x_{bs}+\sum_{b\subseteq(p^\ell,1],s}y_{i_s}x_{bs}\)

definitions.name: Sharp joint policy-mean set
definitions.construction: \(S(q)=\{(\mathbb E[\mathbf 1\{U\le p^\ell\}Y_1+\mathbf 1\{U>p^\ell\}Y_0])_{\ell=1}^L:U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],\ D=\mathbf 1\{U\le p_Z\},\ Y=DY_1+(1-D)Y_0,\ (U,Y_0,Y_1)\perp Z,\ \exists(V_0,V_1)\text{ satisfying existential rank similarity},\ \mathcal L(D,Y\mid Z)=q\}\)

definitions.name: Path-feasibility domains
definitions.construction: \(D_\gamma=\{q\in\overline{\mathcal Q}:q\text{ lies in the closure of order cell }\omega,\ S_\gamma(q)\ne\varnothing\}\quad(\gamma=(\omega,\sigma)\in\Gamma_K)\)

definitions.name: Finite path-survival fan
definitions.construction: \(J=\{\gamma:q_\star\in D_\gamma\}\), \(\mathfrak F(q_\star)\) is the relative sign fan of all inequalities defining \(D_\gamma\) that bind at \(q_\star\), and \(J_F=\{\gamma\in J:F\subseteq T_{D_\gamma}(q_\star)\}\) for every nonempty relative-open face \(F\in\mathfrak F(q_\star)\)

definitions.name: Simultaneous multinomial confidence region
definitions.construction: \(R_n=\{q'\in\Delta_{2K-1}^2:q'_z(d,k)\in I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{zdk}(\alpha/(4K))\ \text{for every }(z,d,k)\}\), with the full arm simplex used when its sample count is zero

definitions.name: Joint law--allocation inversion systems
definitions.construction: For every \(\gamma=(\omega,\sigma)\in\Gamma_K\), \(\mathcal P_\gamma=\{(q',x):q'\in R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap\overline\omega,\ A_\gamma x=b_\gamma+B_\gamma q',\ x\ge0\}\).

definitions.name: Outer-set and set-of-sets inversion
definitions.construction: \(C_n=\bigcup_{q'\in R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}}S(q')\), \(\mathcal H_n=\{S(q'):q'\in R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}\}\); if \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}=\varnothing\), set \(C_n=[y_1,y_K]^L\) and let \(\mathcal H_n\) contain every nonempty compact subset of \([y_1,y_K]^L\)

definitions.name: Outer-set and set-of-sets Hausdorff radii
definitions.construction: When \(\mathcal H_n\ne\varnothing\), define \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}=\sup_{A\in\mathcal H_n}d_H(C_n,A)\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}=\inf_{A\in\mathcal H_n}\sup_{B\in\mathcal H_n}d_H(A,B)\). Under the empty-intersection fallback, set \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}=y_K-y_1\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}=(y_K-y_1)/2\).

definitions.name: Finite common-rank inversion algorithm
definitions.construction: Given \(K,L,y,p^{1:L},N,\alpha\), all endpoints of \(I^{\mathrm{CP}}_{zdk}\), and the arrays \(A_\gamma,B_\gamma,b_\gamma,C_\gamma\), enumerate \(\Gamma_K=\Omega(p^{1:L})\times\Sigma_K\); construct every \(\mathcal P_\gamma\); output \(C_n=\bigcup_\gamma\{C_\gamma x:(q',x)\in\mathcal P_\gamma\}\) and the common-parameter representation of \(\mathcal H_n\); encode \(d_H\le r\), \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}\), and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}\) as quantified linear-real formulas over these systems; eliminate quantifiers and isolate the relevant infimum or supremum boundary in \(r\). Let \(v_{\mathrm{alg}}\) and \(m_{\mathrm{alg}}\) be, respectively, the largest numbers of real variables and scalar affine atoms in any generated formula.

definitions.name: Exact-face model projection
definitions.construction: \(T=T_E(q_\star)\), \(P_E(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E}\|u-v\|_2\), and \(\widetilde q=P_E(\widehat q)\)

definitions.name: Relative-face Gaussian first-stage object
definitions.construction: \(\Sigma_z=\{\operatorname{diag}(q_{\star z})-q_{\star z}q_{\star z}^{\mathsf T}\}/\pi_z\) after deletion of structural-zero and normalization directions, and \(G\sim N_T(0,\Sigma)\)

definitions.name: Projected full-loss germ handle
definitions.construction: Compile the finite semilinear graph of \(f(u,q)=d_H(S(P_Eu),S(q))\) by pathwise primal--dual elimination; substitute \(u=q\) into every cell boundary and affine value intercept; normalize these diagonal forms; snap forms within \(\kappa_n\) of zero with \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\) and \(\sqrt n\kappa_n\to\infty\); restrict all incident pieces and Gaussian draws to \(T\)

statements.statement: Every observed law generated by latent-index monotone selection, uniform \(U\), exclusion, and instrument independence satisfies, for each \(k=1,\ldots,K\), \[c_{0k}=\Pr(p_0<U\le p_1,Y_0=y_k)\ge0,\qquad c_{1k}=\Pr(p_0<U\le p_1,Y_1=y_k)\ge0.\] Hence \(q\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\), and these inequalities are observable compatibility checks rather than maintained assumptions.
statements.justification: The lemma separates testable observed-law implications of monotone selection from the maintained latent model.
statements.gap: The principal-stratum inequalities are standard, but recording them as derived compatibility restrictions prevents the observed law from being assumed compatible by fiat.
statements.consumer: Every path-feasibility and confidence-region computation can reject incompatible observed laws before solving allocation systems.

statements.statement: Every law satisfying existential rank similarity has a rank-invariant replacement with one \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and potential outcomes \((Q_0(V),Q_1(V))\) that preserves \(\mathcal L(Y_d\mid U)\) for \(d\in\{0,1\}\), the observed law \(q\), and every policy mean on \(p^{1:L}\).
statements.justification: This reduction turns existential conditional rank equality into a single ordered support without imposing an independent probability-integral-transform jitter.
statements.gap: Marx uses rank similarity for sharp policy bounds, but the finite-alphabet joint construction with missing complier support is not stated as this replacement lemma.
statements.consumer: The common rank makes joint policy compatibility enumerable by finitely many chains.

statements.statement: On every weak-order cell \(\omega\in\Omega(p^{1:L})\), \[S(q)=\bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma_K}S_{(\omega,\sigma)}(q)=\bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma_K}\{C_{(\omega,\sigma)}x:A_{(\omega,\sigma)}x=b_{(\omega,\sigma)}+B_{(\omega,\sigma)}q,\ x\ge0\},\qquad |\Sigma_K|=\binom{2K-2}{K-1}.\] At a propensity--grid tie, adjacent order labels give duplicate boundary images, so the same bound holds for distinct images. Every feasible allocation is attained by one law satisfying the maintained model, and membership failure has one Farkas certificate for every path. Within the fixed finite outcome alphabet, the characterization remains valid when complier support is not full and supplies the joint policy set in that missing-support direction.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the entire simultaneous policy curve rather than separately sharp coordinates.
statements.gap: Within the fixed finite outcome alphabet, Marx's Proposition 5 relies on full complier support; generic discrete instrumental-variable programs do not encode the common ordered rank across all latent-index bins.
statements.consumer: Oregon Medicaid analysts can reject simultaneous discounted-take-up and never-treated extrapolations that pass every coordinatewise bound.

statements.statement: When the complier outcome support is full and closed in the population support, every coordinate projection of \(S(q)\) equals the corresponding uniformly sharp rank-similar counterfactual-average interval in Marx's Proposition 5; for \(K=2\), the path representation reduces to the two monotone common-rank paths.
statements.justification: The reduction anchors the new representation to the published full-support benchmark.
statements.gap: The published benchmark does not supply the finite-alphabet joint set or its path decomposition when complier support is incomplete.
statements.consumer: Applied users recover the familiar Marx intervals whenever the empirical support condition is credible.

statements.statement: For the \(K=3\) law in the witness construction, \[S_0=\{(1+x,1,1+z):|x|\le1/8,\ |z|\le1/8,\ xz\le0\}.\] Each of the six path images is attained by one legal law, while \((9/8,1,9/8)\notin S_0\) has six full-system Farkas certificates. Hence separate coordinatewise upper endpoints and convexified support functions are not jointly sharp.
statements.justification: A concrete nonconvex set makes the common-law restriction empirically distinguishable from marginal envelopes.
statements.gap: Existing finite programs characterize convex latent-distribution images; this witness isolates the additional common-rank chain obstruction.
statements.consumer: The witness is a reproducible diagnostic for implementations that accidentally convexify joint policy conclusions.

statements.statement: For every legal \(q_\star\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\), the following are equivalent: \(S\) is Hausdorff continuous at \(q_\star\) relative to \(\overline{\mathcal Q}\); for every feasible nonzero face \(F\in\mathfrak F(q_\star)\), \[S(q_\star)=\bigcup_{\gamma\in J_F}S_\gamma(q_\star);\] and there exist \(\varepsilon,H>0\) such that \[d_H(S(q),S(q_\star))\le H\|q-q_\star\|\] for every \(q\in\overline{\mathcal Q}\) with \(\|q-q_\star\|<\varepsilon\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives a finite observable-law frontier separating regular and discontinuous sharp policy sets.
statements.gap: Beresteanu--Molinari and Chernozhukov--Hong--Tamer do not treat components whose feasibility domains disappear inside a nonconvex union.
statements.consumer: The criterion determines when a regular plug-in policy-set analysis is locally defensible and when global inversion is required.

statements.statement: For the witness family, \[S_t=\{(7/8,s,9/8+2t):1\le s\le1+2t\}\quad(0<t<1/4),\qquad d_H(S_t,S_0)=1/4+2t,\] and with \(\pi_0=\pi_1=1/2\), \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{q_0},P_{q_t})=-\tfrac18\log(1-16t^2).\] For \(t_n=1/n\), the \(n\)-sample total variation distance vanishes while the sharp sets remain at Hausdorff distance tending to \(1/4\). Therefore no estimator is uniformly Hausdorff consistent on the model, and every uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest random collection containing \(S(q)\) has Hausdorff diameter at least \(1/4-o(1)\) with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\) along one of these laws.
statements.justification: The causal discontinuity is converted into a statistical impossibility under fixed positive principal shares and fixed observed support.
statements.gap: General uniform-inference papers motivate nearby-law analysis but do not provide this rank-similar set-separation experiment.
statements.consumer: The lower bound prevents misleading globally shrinking policy-set error bars in Medicaid extrapolation.

statements.statement: For the finite inputs \(K,L,y,p^{1:L},N,\alpha\), the \(4K\) Clopper--Pearson intervals, and the generated component arrays \(A_\gamma,B_\gamma,b_\gamma,C_\gamma\), the finite common-rank inversion algorithm terminates and returns: an exact finite-union extended formulation of \(C_n\); an exact common-parameter finite-union representation of every member of \(\mathcal H_n\); and the exact radii \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}\). Its outputs equal the objects in the outer-inversion and inversion-radii definitions, including the deterministic fallback when \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}=\varnothing\). In the unit-cost ordered-field model it uses at most \[(2m_{\mathrm{alg}}|\Gamma_K|)^{2^{O(v_{\mathrm{alg}})}}\] arithmetic and order operations, where \(|\Gamma_K|\le(2L+1)^2\binom{2K-2}{K-1}\); hence the procedure is finite for every fixed input.
statements.justification: The theorem turns the nonconvex path representation into a terminating exact procedure for both reported confidence objects and their metric informativeness.
statements.gap: Finite categorical instrumental-variable programs handle one convex compatibility region; they do not compute Hausdorff radii for a common-parameter collection of law-dependent nonconvex path unions.
statements.consumer: Oregon Medicaid analysts can compute exact outer regions and diagnose their Hausdorff width before reporting extrapolations at support boundaries.

statements.statement: As a corollary of observed-law coverage and the inversion definitions, \(q\in R_n\) implies \(S(q)\subseteq C_n\) and \(S(q)\in\mathcal H_n\). Therefore, for every \(n\) and every compatible law, \[\Pr_q\{S(q)\subseteq C_n\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad \Pr_q\{S(q)\in\mathcal H_n\}\ge1-\alpha.\] These inclusions remain valid on structural-zero faces, when an instrument arm has zero sample count, and when empirical cell differences are incompatible with monotonicity.
statements.justification: The corollary records the finite-sample honesty inherited directly from simultaneous multinomial coverage.
statements.gap: Romano--Shaikh supplies the general inversion logic; the corollary specializes it to the common-rank path correspondence and its set-of-sets image.
statements.consumer: Policy analysts retain finite-sample-valid outer conclusions wherever local Gaussian calibration is uncertified.

statements.statement: At every \(q_\star\) satisfying the equivalent conditions of the continuity frontier on a specified sampling face \(E\), does the projected full-loss germ handle consistently recover all and only the zero-intercept homogeneous pieces of \(f(q_\star+v,q_\star)\) on every feasible \(v\in T\), including continuous multi-path switches and propensity--grid ties, so that \[\sqrt n\,d_H(S(\widetilde q),S(q_\star))\Rightarrow\psi_{q_\star}(G)\] and Gaussian simulation of the recovered germ gives pointwise asymptotically valid Hausdorff balls?
statements.justification: This is the nonroutine inference step: path labels alone do not determine the active Hausdorff-loss pieces.
statements.gap: Fang--Santos presumes access to a consistently estimable directional map, while Kaido--Molinari--Stoye treats smooth projections rather than law-dependent unions on relative faces.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields root-\(n\) calibrated metric inference at certified regular Oregon-type laws without claiming global regularity.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(t_0\in(0,1/4)\) in the witness submodel, the unique surviving path satisfies \(d_H(S_s,S_t)=2|s-t|\) locally. With \(\widehat t=\{\widehat q_1(1,3)-\widehat q_1(1,1)\}/2\), \[\sqrt n\,d_H(S_{\widehat t},S_{t_0})\Rightarrow2\sqrt{1/4-2t_0^2}\,|N(0,1)|.\] Plug-in folded-normal quantiles give pointwise first-order Hausdorff coverage.
statements.justification: The solved one-path stratum verifies that the regular branch is nonvacuous while leaving the multi-path recovery theorem open.
statements.gap: Generic nonsmooth-bound asymptotics do not state this explicit rank-policy folded-normal loss law.
statements.consumer: The proposition supplies a calibration benchmark and a mandatory regression test for the full loss compiler.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the observed binary-instrument experiment with fixed \(\pi_z>0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Instrument arms have positive probabilities; treatment overlap outside \([p_0,p_1]\) is not imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are estimated by armwise empirical proportions and projected onto \(\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E\) only for the certified regular branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Uniformly sharp rank-similar counterfactual-average bounds rely on full complier support.
Aumann-expectation identification regions admit Hausdorff-consistent estimation and set-valued limit theory.
Criterion-minimizer identified sets admit Hausdorff-rate and confidence-region analysis.
Test inversion can cover an entire identified set uniformly under stated conditions.
Ordinary-bootstrap validity under Gaussian limits is equivalent to full Hadamard differentiability.
Calibrated projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions in moment-inequality models.
Sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds can have nonstandard limits and ordinary-bootstrap failure.
Categorical instrumental-variable compatibility and confidence inversion reduce to finite convex programs.
Discrete structural instrumental-variable functions are generally set identified and support sensitive.

tldr: A binary instrument identifies complier outcome distributions but policies below \(p_0\) and above \(p_1\) require extrapolation. Under exactly Marx's existential rank similarity and a fixed finite ordered outcome alphabet, the sharp simultaneous policy-mean set is a finite nonconvex union of common-rank path images, each attained by one law. The comparison to Marx is confined to this finite-alphabet extension in the missing-complier-support direction, and the observable monotonicity inequalities are derived from the latent model. Path survival gives the exact Hausdorff continuity frontier and a centered local Lipschitz bound. A legal three-outcome contiguous submodel proves that globally honest metric procedures cannot shrink uniformly. A terminating finite algorithm computes the multinomial outer set, the set-of-sets image, and their exact Hausdorff radii; finite-sample coverage is the direct inversion corollary. The paper's open statistical kernel is recovery of the complete projected Hausdorff-loss germ on every certified continuous sampling face.

project_justification.gap: Marx's full-support condition makes rank-similar groupwise extrema jointly attainable. Within the fixed finite-alphabet setting, allowing missing complier support leaves no published sharp joint policy-grid set, no stability criterion for disappearing common-rank couplings, and no finite procedure computing Hausdorff radii for the resulting set-of-sets inversion.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes convert existential common ranks into finitely many ordered chains, but the resulting set is a law-dependent nonconvex union rather than one convex program or one smooth projection.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the observable compatibility inequalities from the maintained latent model and supplies a sharp path-union representation, finite exclusion certificates, an if-and-only-if continuity frontier, a contiguous impossibility theorem, a terminating exact inversion-and-radius algorithm, the accompanying finite-sample coverage corollary, and a concrete full-loss germ handle for the remaining regular-calibration question.

related_work: Marx (2024) is the direct substantive anchor: Proposition 5 obtains uniformly sharp rank-similar policy bounds under full complier support, and footnote 29 identifies the construction that fails without it. The path theorem addresses that missing-support direction for a fixed finite outcome alphabet, so the comparison is directional rather than a model-class inclusion. Imbens and Rubin (1997) give the principal-stratum interpretation underlying the observable monotonicity inequalities; here those inequalities are derived as compatibility checks. Chesher (2010), Torgovitsky (2019), and Han and Yang (2024) show how discrete structural restrictions can be encoded by finite feasibility or linear programs; they inform the allocation representation but do not impose one common ordered rank across every latent-index bin. Beresteanu and Molinari (2008) and Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) provide regular Hausdorff theory for different set-valued substrates; the survival theorem addresses law-dependent component death in a nonconvex union. Romano and Shaikh (2010) motivate the coverage corollary through general identified-set inversion. Song et al. (2026) informs the finite categorical feasibility layer, while the algorithm theorem adds common-parameter nonconvex unions and exact outer-set and hyperspace Hausdorff radii. Fang and Santos (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Fan and Park (2010) motivate the active-germ problem, but none proves recovery of the complete projected Hausdorff-loss partition on structural-zero faces.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact bottleneck is not generic directional differentiation. The full projected Hausdorff loss can change affine pieces while every path domain remains unchanged. A valid proof must compile boundary and value-intercept forms, include model projection, snap their diagonal zero sets, and verify the same homogeneous germ on all relative tangent faces. A path-domain-only bootstrap is insufficient.
honest_scope: The path representation is scoped to a fixed finite outcome alphabet and the missing-complier-support direction relative to Marx's full-support result; the comparison is not a model-class inclusion. The finite survival criterion, centered Lipschitz implication, three-outcome discontinuity, impossibility argument, and exact finite inversion-and-radius algorithm are theorem targets with concrete proof architectures. The inequalities \(c_0\ge0\) and \(c_1\ge0\) are derived observed-law compatibility checks, not maintained assumptions. Simultaneous coverage is a direct corollary of observed-law coverage and the inversion definitions, not a headline theorem, and no finite-sample optimality is claimed. Pairwise-neighborhood Lipschitz continuity, a globally continuous derivative, and globally shrinking honest Hausdorff inference are not claimed. The general active-stratum calibration is explicitly open; only the interior one-path folded-normal case is posed as a closed benchmark. Under full complier support the coordinate projections must reduce to Marx's Proposition 5, and for \(K=2\) only the two monotone paths remain.

seed_details.title: Finite-alphabet common-rank path representation with missing complier support
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Assumption 4(a); Lemma 4; Proposition 5 and its proof; footnote 29; Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Within a fixed finite outcome alphabet, replace groupwise quantile envelopes that require full complier support by a sharp joint policy-grid set attained by one latent law.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The jointly attainable groupwise extremizers in Marx's Lemma 4 must be replaced by one common chain of outcome pairs across every latent-index bin.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-alphabet common-rank lattice paths, rank-similar joint policy sets, and rank similarity with missing complier support found no matching theorem.
seed_details.red_team_objection: The result is immediate from Marx's Proposition 5 because his bounds are uniformly sharp.
seed_details.rebuttal: Proposition 5 invokes full complier support, and footnote 29 states that both the bounding quantiles and the joint extremal construction must change without it.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses the coupling-native M10 representation rather than defaulting to one convex program; one-law attainment and the inference rung prevent an identification-only analogue.

seed_details.title: Necessary-and-sufficient path-survival frontier for Hausdorff continuity
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; identification-region representation; Hausdorff consistency and limit-theory results; concluding discussion
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize continuity of a law-dependent nonconvex union whose components can disappear even when all multinomial cells move continuously.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Componentwise Hausdorff control must be supplemented by a finite comparison between base images and paths surviving along every feasible tangent face.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches joining Hausdorff continuity, rank similarity, and finite polytope unions returned no econometric characterization of path survival.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Continuity follows mechanically from fixed-matrix linear-program sensitivity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Fixed-path fibers are Lipschitz, but an entire path image can vanish; the missing reverse inclusion is exactly the nonconvex survival condition.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Both necessity and sufficiency are required, and the centered Lipschitz statement is not inflated into pairwise neighborhood regularity.

seed_details.title: Contiguous path-drop impossibility paired with computable honest inversion
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Lemma 2.1; Theorems 2.2--2.4; empirical illustration; final appendix argument
seed_details.opportunity: Separate uniform coverage from uniform informativeness when the sharp causal set itself jumps along statistically indistinguishable laws.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Generic test inversion must be preceded by a two-law experiment proving that no globally honest Hausdorff procedure can shrink uniformly.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for rank-similar identified-set discontinuity and uniformly shrinking Hausdorff confidence regions found no specialized impossibility-and-inversion pair.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Romano and Shaikh already provide uniform confidence regions for identified sets.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their coverage theory does not characterize non-shrinkage forced by a discontinuous causal correspondence or exploit finite common-rank feasibility for exact outer inversion.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The impossibility is paired with a positive globally honest procedure and is based on a legal contiguous submodel rather than a degenerate isolated law.

seed_details.title: Projected full-loss germ recovery on certified continuity strata
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorems 3.1--3.3; convex-set projection application; Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Recover every active zero-intercept piece of projected Hausdorff loss before simulating the Gaussian directional limit.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derivative evaluation must be replaced by full semilinear loss-partition compilation and diagonal-stratum recovery on the relative multinomial tangent space.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Hausdorff loss of finite polytope unions and derivative bootstrap on structural-zero faces found no complete germ-recovery theorem.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Fang and Santos make the calibration automatic once directional differentiability is stated.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their resampling theorem requires the correct derivative; here both the component domain and projected max-min loss partition are law-dependent, so recovering that derivative is the unresolved theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit law is the native M11(c) shape; no minimax converse is added merely to mimic the cluster default, and the open handle specifies the full-loss compiler.

seed_details.title: Finite certificates for nonconvex joint policy incompatibility
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorems 1--3 and their finite Strassen construction; convex inference program; Section 8 Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Give pathwise Farkas certificates showing why separately feasible policy coordinates need not be jointly attainable.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A single convex feasibility system must become one certificate per common-rank path because support functions retain only the convex hull.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Farkas certificates for joint rank-similar policy curves found no direct match.
seed_details.red_team_objection: This is only routine duality after discretization.
seed_details.rebuttal: The certificate family is useful but subordinate; the novel object is the common-law nonconvex union, not Farkas duality itself.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not promoted as a standalone contribution because finite duality without the path-union theorem would be routine.

seed_details.title: Grid-refinement coherence of common-law policy sets
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 2.2; Proposition 5; proof by integrated quantiles; Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Show that refining the threshold grid and projecting back leaves the sharp joint set unchanged.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Uniform bounds indexed by one policy weight must be replaced by a common attained law evaluated simultaneously on nested grids.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for projective coherence of finite rank-similar policy sets found no named result.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Projection coherence is immediate after a one-law attainment theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds once the path representation is proved, so this is a corollary rather than an independent seed.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is dropped rather than padded into a separate theorem-level novelty claim.

seed_details.title: Set-of-sets inference for discontinuous sharp correspondences
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorems 1--3; convex inference program; Section 8 Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Map a finite-sample multinomial law region through every common-rank path to cover either the sharp set or the set of admissible sharp sets.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A convex functional of one categorical-IV polytope must be replaced by inversion over a nonconvex union and a hyperspace-valued target.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-sample set-of-sets inversion in rank-similar policy models found no match.
seed_details.red_team_objection: Coverage is a tautological image of an observed-law confidence region.
seed_details.rebuttal: The coverage inclusion is retained only as a corollary; the substantive theorem is the terminating exact computation of the nonconvex outer set, the common-parameter set-of-sets image, and both Hausdorff radii.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The generic coverage step is explicitly demoted, while the algorithm has finite inputs, certified termination, exact output semantics, and a real-arithmetic complexity bound.

seed_details.title: Critical support-deficit frontier for the first disappearing common-rank path
seed_details.opportunity: Parametrize missing complier atoms and derive the first value at which a policy conclusion loses joint attainability.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The support restriction must enter path-feasibility inequalities rather than only marginal quantile envelopes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for a critical support deficit under rank similarity found no established scalar frontier.
seed_details.red_team_objection: No invariant scalar deficit orders multidimensional missing-support patterns.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is decisive without a policy-specific direction, which would narrow the general joint-set question.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A critical scalar is not invented when the multidimensional substrate does not support an invariant M3 frontier.

seed_details.title: Generic non-shrinkage lower bounds near path-drop faces
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorems 2.2--2.4; uniform-coverage construction; empirical illustration; appendix proof
seed_details.opportunity: Strengthen one contiguous witness into a uniform lower bound over a class of path-drop faces.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Moment-selection sequences must be replaced by latent allocations whose observed laws are contiguous while their sharp policy sets stay separated.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for generic path-drop lower bounds under rank similarity found no direct theorem.
seed_details.red_team_objection: A generic region of discontinuities is incompatible with the polyhedral faces on which path death occurs.
seed_details.rebuttal: A relative-face uniform class may be possible, but the present evidence proves only a legal contiguous submodel, so the generic strengthening is not promised.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal retains the exact witness but does not mislabel it as a generic-region theorem.

literature_map.settled: Marx gives sharp rank-similar policy bounds under full complier support; Chesher, Torgovitsky, and Han--Yang establish finite or linear feasibility methods for discrete structural models.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: None of the opened results gives, on a fixed finite outcome alphabet, a one-law finite union indexed by common-rank paths when full complier support fails.

literature_map.settled: Existing results control regular set-valued expectations, criterion-minimizer sets, or fixed directionally differentiable maps.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No opened paper characterizes continuity of a law-dependent finite union by necessary-and-sufficient component survival.

literature_map.settled: Derivative resampling, calibrated projection, nonsmooth sharp-bound limits, and finite categorical multinomial inversion are available separately.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The complete projected Hausdorff-loss partition and its snapped homogeneous germ on structural-zero tangent faces are not supplied by those results.
